messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: normal_cdf with vector input?
parts:
Hi!

I am a bit confused at what the output of the normal_cdf function is when you give it vectors as inputs. The signature according to the doc is

real normal_cdf(reals y, reals mu, reals sigma)

So the input can be vectors, but the output is always a single number - what is that single number when I input vectors??? I would expect to get back a vector when I input a vector...

BTW, it would be nice for users to point out in the manual at the normal_cdf doc that you can actually approximate this function in log-space very well using the Phi_approx function approach (log_inv_logit). This gave me much better model runs for left-censored data due to the improved numerical stability.

Sebastian

On Mar 16, 2016, at 6:19 AM, Sebastian Weber <sdw....@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi!

I am a bit confused at what the output of the normal_cdf function is when you give it vectors as inputs. The signature according to the doc is

real normal_cdf(reals y, reals mu, reals sigma)

So the input can be vectors, but the output is always a single number - what is that single number when I input vectors??? I would expect to get back a vector when I input a vector...

It evaluates the cdf of every input (broadcast, if necessary) and returns the product. 

The log pdfs return a sum, the cdfs return a product since its in linear space.

BTW, it would be nice for users to point out in the manual at the normal_cdf doc that you can actually approximate this function in log-space very well using the Phi_approx function approach (log_inv_logit). This gave me much better model runs for left-censored data due to the improved numerical stability.

Sebastian

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: normal_cdf with vector input?
parts:
On Wednesday, March 16, 2016 at 12:19:00 PM UTC+2, Sebastian Weber wrote:
BTW, it would be nice for users to point out in the manual at the normal_cdf doc that you can actually approximate this function in log-space very well using the Phi_approx function approach (log_inv_logit). This gave me much better model runs for left-censored data due to the improved numerical stability.

Using logit is close to using student_t_cdf with degrees of freedom nu=7. Switching from normal to something with thicker tails may also explain the improved stability.

Aki

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: normal_cdf with vector input?
parts:
Hi!

@ Daniel: Thanks for the clarification; makes sense wrt to how normal_log is defined.

@ Aki: Maybe I was imprecise. The unit normal CDF can be approximated with (according to the Stan user manual)

Phi_approx„(x)… ƒ = logit^{-1}(0.07056 * x^3 ‚ + 1.5976 * x)…

Now, this can be used for a much improved (approximate) version of normal_cdf_log, since it won't under- or overflow so quickly. Robustness via a student_t or any other distributions would be a different approach which I haven't tried back then, but the above works splendid (in particular with ADVI which does not like NaNs so much, at least in the past). All I wanted to say is that putting a note in the manual besides the normal_cdf (where you warn about the numerical issues due to over+underflow) would be helpful for users who wonder how they may get around these numerical challenges.

Sebastian
